text:
$$\exists K\in\mathbb N\ \forall n,k\in\mathbb N:\ 0<k,\ k^2\le n,\ n<k\bigl(k+3k^{21/40}\bigr),\ k\lfloor n/k\rfloor \mid k!,\ \operatorname{minFac}\binom nk>\lfloor n/k\rfloor\ \Longrightarrow\ k\le K.$$

In words: only finitely many $k$ admit an $n$ in the strip $k^2\le n<k(k+3k^{0.525})$ (the inequality is taken over the reals, with $21/40$ a real exponent) such that $k\cdot\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ divides $k!$ and the least prime factor of $\binom nk$ exceeds $\lfloor n/k\rfloor$.

Lean conventions: `n / k` is floor division; `Nat.minFac` is 1 at 1 (and 2 at 0); `0 < k` is a hypothesis.
label: the thin strip above k²
